implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.py defines BOARD_SIZE = 8; Board.__init__ creates a size‑by‑size grid of EMPTY cells.
Board._setup_initial_position() in game_logic.py places the standard four discs in the centre.
Game.__init__ sets current_player = BLACK and _advance_turn() swaps between BLACK and WHITE.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Valid‑move detection in all eight directions
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.get_discs_to_flip() scans BOARD_DIRECTIONS and returns discs to flip; Board.is_valid_move() uses it.
Board.make_move() flips all positions returned by get_discs_to_flip() and updates the grid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Automatic pass when a player has no legal moves
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._advance_turn() checks opponent moves; if none, it sets pass_message and does not change current_player.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game‑over detection (board full or no moves for both)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_game_over() returns True when board.is_full() or neither side has valid moves; Game._advance_turn() sets game_over.
Board.get_score() counts BLACK and WHITE discs; gui._draw_info_panel() renders the scores.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical display of board, discs, hints, last move, and messages
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py draws the grid, discs, hint circles for legal moves, a gold rectangle for the last move, and an info panel with turn/message text.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Mouse click handling to place discs
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameGUI._on_click() translates mouse coordinates to board coordinates and calls Game.try_move().
GameGUI._spawn_flip_animations() creates animation dicts; _draw_flipping_disc() renders the squashing effect over FLIP_FRAMES.
Pressing 'R' triggers GameGUI._restart(), which calls Game.restart() and clears animations.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Entry point to run the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines main() that creates GameGUI and calls run(); guarded by if __name__ == "__main__".

critical_issues: The code depends on the external pygame library; if pygame is not installed the program will not run.

No explicit handling for the case where the current player has no moves at the start of their turn (the UI will just show the pass message after the previous move). This is a minor UX issue, not a rule violation.
judge.summary: The submitted source files contain a complete, functional implementation of Reversi/Othello. All core mechanics—board setup, move validation, disc flipping, turn alternation, pass handling, game‑over detection, scoring, and a pygame GUI with animations—are present and demonstrably coded. The only notable risk is the external pygame dependency, but assuming it is available the program should execute correctly. Verdict: pass.
